hints.title: Closest Heater Distance Minimization
hints.text: Every house must be covered by at least one heater. The minimal radius must cover the house furthest from its nearest heater.

hints.title: Sorted Range Closest Point Lookups
hints.text: Sort the heaters array. For each house, use interval bisection to find the closest heater to its left and right.

hints.title: Global Maximum of Minimal Distances
hints.text: For house h, compute min(abs(h - left_heater), abs(h - right_heater)). The final radius is the maximum across all houses.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def findRadius(self, houses: List[int], heaters: List[int]) -> int:
        heaters.sort()
        res = 0
        for h in houses:
            idx = bisect.bisect_left(heaters, h)
            d1 = abs(h - heaters[idx - 1]) if idx > 0 else float("inf")
            d2 = abs(h - heaters[idx]) if idx < len(heaters) else float("inf")
            res = max(res, min(d1, d2))
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O((M + N) log M) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing every house against every heater takes quadratic O(N * M) time, timing out for 25000 elements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting heaters takes O(M log M) and each house binary search takes O(log M), achieving near-linear performance.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle boundary cases where house lies outside the entire heater range.
